title: Self-Control
definition: Self-Control is Spirit-enabled restraint and disciplined obedience in desires, words, habits, and actions.
summary: Grace trains believers to live with godly discipline rather than being ruled by desires.
christFocus: Jesus Christ gives freedom from slavery to sin and forms disciplined holiness in His people by the Spirit.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Self-Control describes a Spirit-formed pattern of life for those who belong to Jesus Christ. Christian living is not an attempt to earn salvation but the grateful response of people who have been saved by grace and called to walk with the Lord.

Scripture presents this truth so believers can grow in holiness, endurance, love, wisdom, worship, and mission. It touches the heart, the mind, the tongue, relationships, daily habits, and faithful obedience in ordinary life.

The emphasis of this doctrine is grace trains believers to live with godly discipline rather than being ruled by desires.. It points disciples away from self-reliance and toward abiding dependence on Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because discipleship can become shallow when it is reduced to information, emotion, or outward activity alone. Self-Control teaches believers how grace becomes visible in daily conduct, perseverance, relationships, and obedience to Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask the Lord to form this truth in you through Scripture, prayer, repentance, and faithful practice. Let self-control shape how you think, speak, serve, endure, forgive, and represent Christ in the places God has assigned to you.
